rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man arrives during Moses’ exchange with the Egyptian, whose dialogue is omitted because a more important event interrupts the story.
rows.anchor: جاء على حين محاورة القبطي مع موسى فلذلك انطوى أمر محاورتهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city’s far end was likely Pharaoh’s palace quarter; rulers lived at city edges for safety from revolt or raids and easier escape, explaining the messenger’s location.
rows.anchor: أن أقصى المدينة هو ناحية قصور فرعون وقومه فإن عادة الملوك السكنى في أطراف المدن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Tammam’s line about a city center becoming an edge means decline of settlement, a different sense from the city outskirts here.
rows.anchor: كانت هي الوسط المحمي فاتصلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning where the man came from also signals that he knew Moses.
rows.anchor: وجه ذكر المكان الذي جاء منه الرجل وأن الرجل كان يعرف موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-malaʾ means influential people of consequence; here it denotes Pharaoh’s ruling elite, consulting about killing Moses.
rows.anchor: وأراد بهم أهل دولة فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their consultation implies the case reached Pharaoh; Exodus likewise says Pharaoh heard of it and sought Moses’ death.
rows.anchor: وهذا يقتضي أن القضية رفعت إلى فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man hurried to warn Moses because he admired Moses’ uprightness.
rows.anchor: أسرع بالخبر لموسى لأنه كان معجبا بموسى واستقامته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported possibility is that the man belonged to the Children of Israel.
rows.anchor: هذا الرجل من بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is that he was an Egyptian secretly believing; God may have guided his sound nature to recognize idolatry’s corruption and prepared him to save Moses.
rows.anchor: كان من القبط ولكنه كان مؤمنا يكتم إيمانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saʿy is rapid walking; the clause is circumstantial, describing the man who came from the city’s far end.
rows.anchor: وجملة { يسعى } في موضع الحال من { رجل }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaʾtamirūna means consult, with an implied sense of intending; bi marks what they intend to do to Moses.
rows.anchor: قيل : يأتمرون ويهمون بقتلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iʾtimār originally means accepting an order and came to mean consultation because each consultor accepts another’s proposal; Imruʾ al-Qays’s line describes harm from obeying one’s own command.
rows.anchor: ويعدو على المرء ما يأتمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The consultation sense also appears in the command to consult together in what is right.
rows.anchor: ثم شاع إطلاق الائتمار على التشاور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence He said, Moses is a بدل اشتمال of the man’s arrival, since his arrival includes his speaking.
rows.anchor: لأن مجيئه يشتمل على قوله ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destination of the command to leave is omitted but context supplies it: leave the city.
rows.anchor: ومتعلق الخروج محذوف لدلالة المقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assurance of sincere advice explains the command to leave; naṣaḥa commonly takes li, as in the verse about those who advised God and His Messenger, though direct-object usage also occurs.
rows.anchor: لأن أكثر ما يستعمل فعل النصح معدى باللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepositional phrase is brought forward to preserve the verse ending’s cadence.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المجرور للرعاية على الفاصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taraqqub literally means waiting, derives from observing something’s condition, and is metaphorically used here for caution.
rows.anchor: وهو هنا مستعار للحذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ prayer is a بدل اشتمال of his keeping watch, since watchfulness includes praying to God for rescue.
rows.anchor: لأن ترقبه يشتمل على الدعاء إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unjust people are Pharaoh’s people: they were polytheists and sought to kill Moses in retaliation for an accidental killing, which reason and law do not warrant.
rows.anchor: والقوم الظالمون هم قوم فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The episode teaches that God chooses whom He wills, prepares means to fulfill His purpose, and rescues His chosen messenger; upright conduct and love of truth disclose that care to the perceptive observer.
rows.anchor: وأن الناظر البصير في آثار ذلك التدبير يقتبس منها دلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs in Moses’ story invite the Meccans to consider Muhammad’s character and their dealings with him, as the verse asks whether they reason about his lifetime among them.
rows.anchor: وفي ذلك كله مثل للمشركين لو نظروا في حال محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning hints that Muhammad too will leave Mecca and that God will save him from his oppressors.
rows.anchor: إيماء إلى أن رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم سيخرج من مكة

words: مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a separate address to Pharaoh’s courtiers after his exchange with Moses, so the story is joined to the prior scene with a conjunction.
rows.anchor: فهو كلام أقبل به على خطاب أهل مجلسه إثر المحاورة مع موسى

words: مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh tries to secure his courtiers’ belief in his divinity and reject Moses’ teaching that God is Lord of their forefathers and of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: أراد فرعون بخطابه مع ملئه أن يثبتهم على عقيدة إلهيته

words: مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Denying that he knows of another god indirectly denies that one exists: Pharaoh pretends his knowledge covers all truth, so he would know of any rival.
rows.anchor: نفي وجود إله غيره بطريق الكناية يريهم أنه أحاط علمه بكل شيء حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The god denied is Moses’ creator of all; the Egyptians’ supposed gods remain compatible with Pharaoh’s claim because they regarded him as their offspring and essence.
rows.anchor: لأن فرعون عندهم هو مظهر الآلهة المزعومة عندهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh misimagines the Lord of the heavens as residing in the sky, so he orders a tower to reach it and inspect for Moses’ God, claiming firsthand proof against Moses.
rows.anchor: أن يبني له صرحا يبلغ به عنان السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staged search lets Pharaoh pose as a thorough seeker of truth, then use a supposed failed search to increase his courtiers’ confidence that Moses lied; the sophistry exposes their disordered and weak thinking.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا الضغث من الجدل السفسطائي مبلغ من الدلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Haman is the title or name of Pharaoh’s minister.
rows.anchor: لقب أو اسم لوزير فرعون كما تقدم آنفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kindling clay means ordering workers to fire clay into bricks; construction is expressed through its preliminary operation.
rows.anchor: العملة أن يطبخوا الطين ليكون آجرا ويبنوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh begins with the first construction task to start immediately: firing kilns to make bricks, whose base material is called clay.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على العناية بالشروع من أول أوقات الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Brick rather than stone and lime allows a quickly raised tower; durability is irrelevant because it need only be seen before it is abandoned and demolished.
rows.anchor: قصدا للتعجيل بإقامة هذا الصرح المرتفع

rows.speaker: ابن الأثير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Athir says clay replaces everyday terms for brick and tile because those words are too commonplace.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأثير في ( المثل السائر ) :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clearer reason for saying clay is that the word is lighter and more eloquent than the technical word for brick.
rows.anchor: وأظهر من كلام ابن الأثير : أن العدول إلى الطين لأنه أخف وأفصح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing firing to Haman is figurative agency: he orders the work, as one says a ruler built a bridge or al-Mansur built Baghdad.
rows.anchor: باعتبار أنه الذي يأمر بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In earlier monarchies, royal commands passed through ministers, who implemented them using their officials and agents.
rows.anchor: أوامر الملوك في العصور الماضية تصدر بواسطة الوزير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣarḥ means a high palace or elevated building.
rows.anchor: والصرح : القصر المرتفع ، وقد تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s hope of reaching heaven to find Moses’ God rests on false ideas that a tower can reach heaven and that God is located in a heavenly place.
rows.anchor: إذ حسب أن السماء يوصل إليها بمثل هذا الصرح ما طال بناؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iṭṭilāʿ is forceful, effortful ascent undertaken because the task is difficult.
rows.anchor: والاطلاع : الطلوع القوي المتكلف لصعوبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓann here means certainty; Pharaoh’s attempt either strengthens that certainty or is meant to persuade his people.
rows.anchor: استعمل فيه الظن بمعنى القطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh may mislead his people into thinking Moses placed God at a reachable location, then treat not finding Him there as proof that He does not exist.
rows.anchor: ولعله أراد بهذا تمويه الأمر على قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account portrays deviant beliefs as founded on false imaginings and their leaders’ deceptive arguments.
rows.anchor: وكانت دلائلها قائمة على تمويه الدجالين من زعمائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Moses one of the liars casts him as belonging to a group characterized by lying.
rows.anchor: يدل على أنه يعده من الطائفة الذين شأنهم الكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an does not say whether the tower was built; it cannot be one of the pyramids, which were stone tombs rather than brick structures.
rows.anchor: وليس هو أحد الأهرام لأن الأهرام بنيت من حجارة لا من آجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One exegetical report says the tower was completed, Pharaoh climbed it, descended, and claimed he had killed Moses’ God.
rows.anchor: فحكى بعضهم أنه تم وصعد فرعون إلى أعلاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says the unfinished tower collapsed, killing many builders and soldiers.
rows.anchor: وحكى بعضهم أن الصرح سقط قبل إتمام بنائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third report says construction never began; the author postpones his own alternative reading to Sūrat Ghāfir.
rows.anchor: وحكى بعضهم أنه لم يشرع في بنائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes that he will explain another possible meaning of the verse in Sūrat Ghāfir.
rows.anchor: وقد لاح لي في معنى الآية وجه آخر سأذكره في سورة المؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istikbār is more intense than ordinary arrogance: Pharaoh presumptuously imagined he could reach the mighty Lord as a rival or conqueror.
rows.anchor: إذ طمع في الوصول إلى الرب العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His soldiers are followers; their arrogance follows from his because they adopt the beliefs he dictates.
rows.anchor: فاستكباره هو الأصل واستكبار جنوده تبع لاستكباره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth may mean Egypt specifically or the world generally, since Egypt’s people were then the greatest nation.
rows.anchor: كانوا يومئذ أعظم أمم الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting us before they worship emphasizes the disavowal and preserves the verse ending’s cadence.
rows.anchor: للاهتمام بهذا التبرؤ مع الرعاية على الفاصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to those summoned in 28:62; after they realize the rebuke concerns their idols and their leaders begin excusing them, the rebuke continues.
rows.anchor: فإن ذلك النداء كان توبيخا لهم على اتخاذهم آلهة شركاء لله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker is left passive because context makes God clear as the one who spoke.
rows.anchor: لأن الفاعل معلوم مما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command offers them false hope, which is immediately followed by despair.
rows.anchor: والأمر مستعمل في الإطماع لتعقب الإطماع باليأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The partners are attributed to the addressees because they claimed those beings shared divinity with God.
rows.anchor: إضافة الشركاء إلى ضمير المخاطبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their call is an appeal for help based on their worldly belief that the idols intercede; the idols’ failure to answer delivers the intended despair.
rows.anchor: والدعاء دعاء الاستغاثة حسب زعمهم أنهم شفعاؤهم عند الله في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: First reported reading: the phrase coordinates with the idols’ failure; they visually see afterlife punishment shown to them and know their partners cannot help, while the following clause begins independently.
rows.anchor: والرؤية بصرية ، والعذاب عذاب الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Second reading: the conjunction is circumstantial; they have seen the afterlife punishment and are bewildered about escape when told to call their partners, while the next clause is independent.
rows.anchor: أن تكون الواو للحال والرؤية أيضا بصرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Third reading: seeing means knowing, with the second object omitted; they know punishment has overtaken them, and the conjunction may coordinate or mark circumstance.
rows.anchor: أن تكون الرؤية علمية ، وحذف المفعول الثاني اختصارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fourth reading takes لو as a wish expressing regret for their failure to follow guidance in worldly life, which alone could have kept them from punishment.
rows.anchor: فرضها المفسرون : وجماع أقوالهم فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author’s fifth reading takes punishment as worldly: they saw traces of earlier denied nations’ punishment; if they had learned from it and believed the Prophet, they would have abandoned shirk and escaped greater punishment.
rows.anchor: فرضها المفسرون : وجماع أقوالهم فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These several readings all contribute intended meanings, making the verse a concise expression with many meanings.
rows.anchor: فيحتمل معاني كثيرة فرضها المفسرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the first three readings, لو is conditional with an omitted answer supplied by an omitted object of be guided: they would have found escape; كانوا reinforces the proposition, and the imperfect signals guidance now cut off.
rows.anchor: حرف شرط وجوابها محذوفا دل عليه حذف مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the fourth reading, كانوا retains its ordinary past sense, while the imperfect evokes the continuing guidance they regret losing, which must last until life’s end to benefit them.
rows.anchor: حينئذ في موقعه الدال على الاتصاف بالخبر في الماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author’s worldly-punishment reading echoes the reminder that people lived in the dwellings of wrongdoers and saw what God did to them.
rows.anchor: وهذا في معنى قوله تعالى في سورة إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scene from 28:62 is repeated because that day has multiple events and admonition calls for elaborating the grounds of rebuke; this repetition now rebukes denial of messengers after shirk.
rows.anchor: كرر الحديث عنه باعتبار تعدد ما يقع فيه

words: إِنَّ قَٰرُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوْمِ مُوسَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh’s wealthy leaders resisted Muhammad and disparaged poor followers, claiming revelation should come to a wealthy notable; the Qur’an repeatedly rebukes this status-by-wealth assumption.
rows.anchor: من دواعي تصلبهم في إعراضهم عن دعوته اعتزازهم بأموالهم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وغيره
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi reports from Ibn Masʿud and others that Quraysh leaders demanded Muhammad dismiss Khabbab, Bilal, ʿAmmar, and Suhayb so they might follow him; revelation answered that he must not drive away those who call on God. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: روى الواحدي عن ابن مسعود وغيره بأسانيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qarun example follows the reminder that worldly possessions are only the adornment of this life and their owners will be brought before God.
rows.anchor: فيما تقدم من الآيات قريبا قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun’s wealth and arrogance exemplify Meccan figures: Abu Lahab and Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith in kinship and abuse, al-ʿAsi ibn Waʾil in abusing Khabbab, and al-Walid ibn al-Mughira in boasting of wealth and dependents.
rows.anchor: وأن مثل قارون صالح لأن يكون مثلا لأبي لهب

words: إِنَّ قَٰرُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوْمِ مُوسَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story opens as an example for Meccan leaders such as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and Abu Jahl, and attaches to the preceding account of worldly goods and resurrection.
rows.anchor: لذكر قصة ضربت مثلا لحال بعض كفار مكة

words: إِنَّ قَٰرُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوْمِ مُوسَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qarun story also connects with the close of the Pharaoh-soldiers narrative, which ends with the reminder that Muhammad was not at the Mount when God called.
rows.anchor: ولهذه القصة اتصال بانتهاء قصة جند فرعون المنتهية عند قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun is an Arabized form of Hebrew Qorah, altered for easier pronunciation and molded on Arabic names such as Talut and Jalut; its letters are not derived from q-r-n.
rows.anchor: اسم معرب أصله في العبرانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qorah was Moses’ cousin: the source gives their Levi-family genealogies and identifies Izhar as Amram’s brother.
rows.anchor: فهو قورح بن يصهار بن قهات بن لاوى بن يعقوب

rows.speaker: سفر العدد
rows.claim: Numbers 16 says Korah joined 250 Israelite leaders against Moses and Aaron over the Aaronide priesthood, was swallowed by the earth with his followers, and lost his wealth near Jericho; exegetes also say Pharaoh made him Israel’s chief in Egypt and he amassed riches.
rows.anchor: في الإصحاح السادس عشر من سفر العدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’anic account explains Qarun’s envy: Moses’ mission and departure with Israel removed Qarun from power over his people, so he resented Moses.
rows.anchor: لأن موسى لما جاء بالرسالة وخرج ببني إسرائيل زال تأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Storytellers’ elaborate accounts of Qarun’s luxury and magnificence lack Qur’anic or other proof; exegetes repeated them except Ibn ʿAtiyya.
rows.anchor: وقد أكثر القصاص من وصف بذخة قارون وعظمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening إن may emphasize the central lesson about the disastrous end of people deceived by wealth, who fail to thank God, disdain religion, and reject His laws; Qarun’s ancestry itself was not in doubt.
rows.anchor: فمصب التأكيد هو ما بعد قوله

words: إِنَّ قَٰرُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوْمِ مُوسَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, إن draws attention to the whole lesson: Qarun’s belonging to Moses’ people and becoming his enemy is especially striking, even more than Pharaoh’s case.
rows.anchor: لمجرد الاهتمام بالخبر ومناط الاهتمام هو مجموع ما تضمنته القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying Moses’ people rather than Israelites hints at Qarun’s special kinship connection to Moses.
rows.anchor: من الإيماء إلى أن لقارون اتصالا خاصا بموسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is parenthetical between Qarun’s identity and the grant of treasure; fa marks immediate sequence, highlighting how quickly he grew insolent toward his kin after receiving favor.
rows.anchor: وجملة { فبغى عليهم } معترضة بين جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghy is aggression; aggression against a community means slighting its rights, beginning with violation of its law. Oppressing one’s kin is especially painful, as Tarafa’s verse says.
rows.anchor: والاعتداء على الأمة الاستخفاف بحقوقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording about Qarun’s people prepares an analogy with the harm Muhammad suffered from his own idolatrous relatives.
rows.anchor: تمهيد للكناية بهذا الخبر عن إرادة التنظير

words: إِنَّ قَٰرُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوْمِ مُوسَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence happens to scan as a hemistich in al-Khafif meter; Qur’anic rhetorical circumstances can call for wording whose rhythm coincides with a poetic meter.
rows.anchor: فإن هذه الجملة جاءت على ميزان مصراع من بحر الخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basran grammarians allow إن to begin the relative clause of ما; Kufans disallow it and instead parse ما as an indefinite noun described by the following clause, citing lack of Arabic usage.
rows.anchor: عند نحاة البصرة الذين لا يمنعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mafātiḥ is the plural of maftaḥ, the instrument for opening, also called miftāḥ; another plural is mafātīḥ.
rows.anchor: وهو آلة الفتح ، ويسمى المفتاح أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treasures are stored money kept in a box or vault; a store could hold a standard sum, with a key for each container.
rows.anchor: جمع كنز وهو مختزن المال من صندوق أو خزانة

rows.speaker: أبو رزين لقيط بن عامر العقيلي
rows.claim: The Companion Abu Razin said that one key would suffice for Kufa, meaning one treasure could have a single key; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي رزين لقيط بن عامر العقيلي أحد الصحابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many keys imply many vaults and thus great wealth, a two-step metonymy; he also cites a line about a timid dog and thin calf as indirect expression.
rows.anchor: مثل : جبان الكلب مهزول الفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tanūʾ means to weigh heavily; the keys are so heavy that they burden even the strong group carrying them.
rows.anchor: باء الملابسة أن تثقل مع العصبة الذين يحملونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ba is associative, not causal as in Imruʾ al-Qays’s line; the author also rejects al-Zamakhshari’s example in which a load burdens its bearer.
rows.anchor: وليست هذه الباء باء السببية كالتي في قول امرىء القيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects Abu ʿUbayda’s claim that the verse uses reversed syntax.
rows.anchor: فلا يقبله من كان له قلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUṣba means a group; Mujahid’s nearest estimate is ten to fifteen people.
rows.anchor: وأقرب الأقوال في مقدارها قول مجاهد أنه من عشرة إلى خمسة عشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun accumulated his wealth in Egypt and went out with it.
rows.anchor: وكان اكتسب الأموال في مصر وخرج بها
